name: Anatoly Chubais

summary.text: Anatoly Chubais (born 1955) was the Russian official in charge of privatization in the 1990s: deputy prime minister responsible for privatization from 1992, first deputy prime minister in 1994 and again from March 1997 to March 1998, manager of Boris Yeltsin's 1996 re-election campaign, head of the electricity monopoly RAO UES from 1998 to 2008 and of the state nanotechnology corporation Rusnano from 2008 to 2020. He resigned as a presidential special representative and left Russia in March 2022. The Harvard Institute for International Development, funded by USAID, worked closely with Chubais and his associates; a 1996 GAO review examined that programme.

openQuestions: Site claim tested: that the 1995 loans-for-shares auctions, with HIID advisers attached, let insiders acquire Norilsk Nickel, Yukos and Sibneft. Chubais's role as privatization chief is documented; no primary source on the loans-for-shares auctions or on Chubais's specific decisions in them was opened (the only account found was Wikipedia, which is not cited). The site's own caveat that no source shows HIID designed either programme stands.
The 'lax' oversight wording is attributed to the GAO by press reports; the owner may wish to confirm it in the GAO report text.
The claim that Chubais was briefly on the HIID payroll comes from FAIR, an advocacy outlet, and was not confirmed elsewhere.
